title: Rationalize env overlay patterns and modernize Terraform backends & providers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our mono-repo Terraform overlays (env-overlays/*) and a mix of backend configurations have accumulated fragile patterns: ad-hoc per-team overlay patches, duplicated provider pinning, and a single shared S3 backend with noisy statefiles. This increases risk for accidental drift, makes provider upgrades painful, and slows down networking refactors.

Goal: Replace the ad-hoc overlay approach with a small set of supported environment overlay patterns, migrate to per-environment S3 backends with consistent locking (DynamoDB), and standardize AWS provider versions and aliasing to enable a safe v5.x provider upgrade. Reduce noise in networking templates by extracting egress/NAT/EIP lifecycle into a single well-tested module.

Scope & deliverables:
- Design and document two overlay patterns (env-rooted and service-scoped) and migration guidelines in Confluence.
- Introduce a per-environment Terraform backend blueprint (S3 bucket + DynamoDB lock table + encryption) and automated backend bootstrap script.
- Create a new "infra-egress" module that centralizes NAT/EIP lifecycle, cross-account routes, and allows region-aware defaults. Replace duplicated NAT logic in 7 workspaces.
- Pin and test AWS provider v5.8 (minimum) with explicit aliasing for multi-region modules; provide a compatibility shim for v4->v5 breaking changes in a small helper module.
- Update CI (terraform-plan-check) to run isolated plans against the per-env backend using ephemeral workspaces and a smoke test harness.
- Perform state migration steps with a dry-run plan and per-workspace migration PRs; include rollback instructions.

Trade-offs & decisions:
- We deliberately avoid a large one-time rewrite. Plan is incremental: extract modules, migrate 1 region/team at a time. That reduces blast radius at the cost of longer overall migration time.
- Provider shim adds a small maintenance burden but reduces immediate risk for service owners.
- Per-environment backends increase S3/DynamoDB resources but greatly reduce cross-team state contention and make drift isolation easier.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge infra-egress module and run integration tests in dev account. (ETA: 2 weeks)
2) Bootstrapping tooling merged to infra-bootstrap repo and run for staging env (non-prod). (ETA: week 3)
3) Migrate one low-impact production workspace to new backend and provider aliasing, monitor for 48h. (ETA: week 5)
4) Gradual migration of remaining workspaces, with PR checklist and automated plan verification.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: state corruption during S3 backend migration. Mitigation: full state snapshot, dry-run migration PRs, on-call support window during each migration.
- Risk: provider v5 behavior changes. Mitigation: compatibility shim + constrained test matrix in CI + rollout canary per-team.

Next steps (short term):
- Review RFC in Confluence (link below) and get SRE + Platform sign-off on backend blueprint.
- Author infra-egress module and open initial implementation PR targeting dev account.
